# SpeakX · Sia’s October 2026 production calendar

Planning pack, not rendered or published content. All dates and scheduling use Asia/Kolkata (IST). October 1 is Thursday; October 31 is Saturday. The supplied prompts informed this plan; the user’s current direction takes precedence:  Sia alone, varied teaching, selective locations and a full month.

## What ships

- 31 original lessons: 19 A 1/A 2 (61.3%),9 B 1 (29.0%),3 B 2 (9.7%).
- 20 direct-to-camera studio episodes;11 location episodes. Only 5 episodes include a one-second map/pin cutaway.
- 62 primary video placements: 31 Instagram Reels and 31 Facebook videos/Reels.
- 62 X text placements: one morning tip at 08: 30 and one evening exercise at 19: 00 daily. Optional X video replaces an evening text placement; it is not additional base inventory.
- 31 Instagram Story sets at 13: 00 daily, three frames each (93 frames). Facebook Stories remain optional pending account capability and review and are excluded from base counts.
- Base inventory: 155 scheduled units (62 video posts +62 X posts +31 Story sets), or 217 individual posts/frames. This is 31 original lessons, not 155 different lessons.
- 31 word selections are unique within October. The prior word bank was not supplied, so production must check earlier history before certifying the 90-day no-repeat requirement.

## Variety and the reason to return

Sia teaches directly in the studio on 20 days. Eleven lessons use a relevant virtual location; the scene supports the language rather than adding a travel sequence. Location dates areOctober 1,5,8,9,14,15,19,22,23,28,29. The five Thursday dialogue episodes (October 1,8,15,22,29) use Sia’s hook first at 0–2 seconds, a one-second map/pin cutaway at 2–3 seconds, then eye-level Sia alone in the scene. Other location lessons have no map overlay. Studio lessons never have maps.

Maps and addresses have not been supplied. Studio records use `mapPinStatus:  Not used`; location records use `Awaiting map` to record pending location verification. A virtual set may be approved without claiming a real visit. A map-enabled render needs an approved map/pin first; never invent a branch or address. Location codes this month: OFC office/interview;AIR airport. STU means studio, not a physical map category. The larger location library can be added later without forcing a map into every post.

The five learning arcs give a concrete reason to continue:

1. **Oct 1–4: Start speaking.** Introduce yourself, build a simple sentence, repair one missing word and check your progress.
2. **Oct 5–11: Build everyday confidence.** Move from describing confidence to basic grammar, plurals and polite questions.
3. **Oct 12–18: Explain yourself.** Describe a real strength, ask for clarification, give a reason and discuss a topic clearly.
4. **Oct 19–25: Handle work conversations.** Share availability, ask for time on an offer and state a deadline.
5. **Oct 26–31: Speak with flexibility.** Handle changes, past updates, polite disagreement and future plans.

Retention devices rotate: finish a sentence, predict an answer, choose a phrase, hear a before/after correction, reorder blocks, repeat for two seconds, or apply a phrase to a real situation. Each episode provides its answer or worked example; the 13: 00 Story offers another same-day model. Practice is the purpose of the CTA. Viewers can speak privately, write their own example or ask a learning question; do not require comments, tags or shares to unlock teaching.

Every end card names the next day’s specific skill, silently, after the full lesson value. October 31’s November invitation is explicitly proposed; a November calendar has not been approved. These are hypotheses to test through comprehension, saves, completion and repeat viewing—not promises of addictiveness or guaranteed growth.

## Production rules

Revised scripts contain 47–68 spoken words, excluding bracketed directions. Estimate at 1.8 words/second plus explicit practice/quiz pauses, two seconds for transitions/end card, and one additional second only for enabled map cutaways. All estimates are below 45 seconds (maximum 42.8 seconds). Add quiet reading holds or slower target English to achieve 35–45 seconds where shorter. Actual voice renders must be measured. Never speed up English to fit. Bracketed directions and silent cards never enter TTS. The specific next-episode tease is visual, not spoken.

On Mondays the full-word lesson replaces the closing word segment. Other days include a word, Hindi meaning and complete English example. All 31 examples appear literally in their scripts. Wrong English is always marked❌ WRONG from first appearance, including hooks; correct models use✅. Quiz blanks are PRACTICE cards, not model sentences.

Only Sia appears and speaks: her face, hair, grey outfit and warm character-board identity stay locked. No interviewer, staff, classroom children, crowds, reflections or second voice. Dialogue partners appear as silent text cards. Sia_v 1 is a planned voice ID; the character board supplies no audio. Obtain the source voice and documented rights/consent where applicable, then approve the voice test before production. Do not substitute a random voice.

Render a 1920×1080 landscape master and 1080×1920 vertical reframing. Instagram gets vertical; Facebook gets the approved vertical or landscape cut. Deliver subtitles/SRT, transcript, cover, alt text, music rights reference and QA report. Keep essential text, faces and logo outside the bottom 20% and right 12% of vertical layouts. Use the supplied SpeakX logo unchanged on the end card. Warm Hinglish voice, slower English examples, soft original/licensed instrumental under speech, and one gentle answer chime; no sound covers pronunciation.

No unverified user-count, ranking, pricing, outcome or guarantee claims. Scripts and media remain drafts for human language/brand review. Pronunciation spellings are production aids, not formal phonetic transcriptions.

## Scheduling and operations

Weekdays: Instagram 19: 30;Facebook 20: 00. Weekends: Instagram 11: 00;Facebook 11: 30. X daily 08: 30 and 19: 00. Stories daily 13: 00. These are starting hypotheses, not proven best times. Show IST to managers; store UTC in production. Compare performance within a platform, format and consistent metric age.

First batch (Oct 1–4): script lockSep 24, media QASep 28, approvalSep 29. Oct 5–11: production readyOct 1, approvalOct 2. Oct 12–18: readyOct 8, approvalOct 9. Oct 19–25: readyOct 15, approvalOct 16. Oct 26–31: readyOct 22, approvalOct 23. “Ready” includes videos, captions, Story frames and X text. An unapproved slot is skipped and rescheduled through review, never auto-released.

Reports: Oct 5,12,19,26 andNov 2 at 09: 00 IST. Flag immature post data and unavailable metrics. Nov 2’s October report is preliminary; complete the final+30-day cohort afterNov 30. Analytics can propose changes but cannot silently alter approved content. Track series, skill, level, hook type, retention device, setting mode and map use. Compare location versus studio as an experiment, acknowledging topic and weekday confounds; do not claim the scene caused a result from one comparison.

Set:Virtual interview room · OFC · Awaiting map. No map. Start directly with Sia.

Word:**Confident** — aatmavishwasi; sure of your ability. Example:I feel confident today.

Arc:Oct 5–11 · Build everyday confidence: simple grammar, plurals and polite questions.

Retention:Choose the phrase: I feel confident when ___ poora karo. Model answer or worked example is supplied in this episode; no answer is withheld for tomorrow.

**Complete spoken draft**
